notes:
ADVERSARIAL READ vs /images/blueprints/supplier/9ccd5722c833__054Y__3_left_bttn_hole_1_right_bttn_hole.jpg. This is attempt 3; attempt 2 was logged FAIL.

SIDE CONVENTION ESTABLISHED PROGRAMMATICALLY, not guessed. I measured the red-mark centroid in this drawing and in its sibling 0541 ('Left Bttn Hole'). In 0541 the single red mark sits at x=0.689 of image width — the VIEWER'S RIGHT. Since that option is named 'Left', viewer-right = wearer's LEFT in this supplier's lapel drawings. In 054Y the red spans x=0.313 to x=0.712 with three marks clustered at viewer-right and one at viewer-left, which under that convention is three on the wearer's left and one on the wearer's right — exactly what the label says.

COUNTED AT 5x ZOOM on the candidate, both lapels cropped and enlarged side by side: viewer-LEFT lapel carries EXACTLY ONE worked buttonhole; viewer-RIGHT lapel carries EXACTLY THREE, evenly spaced in a vertical column. Under the convention established above that is three on the wearer's left and one on the wearer's right. Correct on both count and side.

ATTEMPTED REJECTIONS THAT FAILED:
(1) Is the viewer-right column actually four buttonholes? At full resolution it is three; what looked like a possible fourth at low magnification is the lapel's own edge stitching.
(2) Mirrored — three on the wrong lapel? No; verified against the measured drawing convention above.
(3) Symmetric pair (the lazy default of putting the same count on both sides)? No — one side has one, the other three.
(4) Annotation colour traced? No. All four buttonholes are tonal navy; there is no red anywhere in frame.
(5) A lapel flower, pin or chain filling a buttonhole and hiding the count? None present.
(6) Wrong lapel style substituted? Notch lapels, matching the drawing.
(7) Any number, arrow or leader line? None.

No critical or major findings.
